To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there was no significant difference between the performances of students from Category A, B, C of SHS in terms of graduating with first class or 2nd Class Upper, (2) the J48 decision tree was the overall best algorithm, (3) the J48 algorithm was more robust and scalable compared with the other two algorithms.

(i) there is a weak correlation between entry grades and final grades of students in the university (ii) students from Category C SHS perform better than students from Category A & B SHS (iii) J48 decision tree is the best algorithm for the classification of students’ data

(1) the J48 algorithm was the most effective in predicting students’ final grades; (2) students from Category C schools performed better than students from Category A or B schools; and (3) there was no strong correlation between SHS aggregate and Final C.W.A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of students based on SHS aggregates.
the application of classification techniques in data mining to predict students’ performance upon graduation using their entry grades.
the use of classification techniques to predict the performance of students in the university based on their entry grades.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the classification technique of data mining has been used to mine data of students to ascertain if there exists any pattern between SHS entry grades with which they entered university and their grades at graduation.

the classification techniques used in the analysis of the data set of Computer Science students at the Kwame Nkumah University of Science & Technology (KNUST) revealed that students who were admitted from Category C SHS performed better than those who were admitted from Categories A and B SHS.
the J48 decision tree is the best classification algorithm for the data mining of the students’ performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the J48 algorithm performed better than the Instance Based Learner (IBL) algorithm and the Multi Layer Perceptrons (MLP) algorithm.
the J48 algorithm was the most accurate in predicting student final CWA.
students from Category B and C SHS performed better in the university compared with their counterpart students from Category A SHS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, there is need for a holistic approach in the admission of students into the University to avoid a situation where the University is flooded with low performing students.
, the classification technique of data mining is an efficient tool to analyze data of student performance.
students who perform poorly in SHS are not necessarily poor students and can still graduate with good grades if they work hard.
